methods.text: not available for Illinois: IDOT publishes costs per person killed or injured, not per crash (2024 Crash Facts p. 23: fatality $2,009,575, A-injury $171,925, B $45,300, C $27,795, property damage crash $6,485, from National Safety Council 2024 estimates); its only per-crash table is 1999-2003, marked 'reference only' (Safety 1-06, p. 225). Pricing a crash by its worst injury with per-person costs would be wrong, so no cost column until IDOT's current HSIP benefit-cost crash costs are found

not available for Illinois: IDOT's only published statewide averages here are fatal and A-injury crashes per 100 centerline miles for rural collectors and local roads (Safety 1-06, p. 7, high-risk rural roads), not crash rates per vehicle-mile; and CrashIQ has no Illinois traffic counts

Highway Safety Manual (AASHTO, 1st, 2010), Ch. 4, Sec. 4.2.3. Illinois's own method, IDOT screens by peer group with frequency, rate and EPDO critical values (Safety 1-06 HSIP candidate form, 'HALIS Peer Group ... Critical Values Exceeded: Freq Rate EPDO', p. 252) and the 5% report; not built, isn't built: this report uses the HSM critical rate against the corridor's own sites (national method)

Safety Engineering Policy Memorandum Safety 1-06, Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP) (Illinois Department of Transportation, effective November 1, 2006 (as posted 2026-11-08)), p. 8: 'five years of crash data should be used for the analysis' (also p. 7 table note: 'a minimum of 5 most recent years of crash data'); written for HSIP analyses
